evidence.requirements: Nearly every functional requirement is met. The start page lists title, date/time, 'EUR n per guest' and 'n seats left' (Home.jsx:32-46, start.jpg). There are 'Book <title>' links (Home.jsx:52), a form with Name/Email/Guests and a 'Book' button (Book.jsx:75-86), and errors under the field (form.jpg). The server enforces the seat limit (app.js:57-64). The confirmation has the heading 'Booking confirmed' plus tasting, guests, total and reference (Confirmation.jsx:33-39, confirmation.jpg). /staff has a 'Password' field and 'Sign in' button checked against STAFF_PASSWORD (Staff.jsx:29-41, index.js:10). Bookings are grouped by tasting with a Cancel button, and cancelling frees seats (app.js:117-133, staff.jpg). The app uses React, Express and react-router. Partial gaps: at 0 seats the page says 'Fully booked' instead of '0 seats left' (api.js:15), which is defensible. No spec, plan or other process artefacts were delivered, even though the brief's Process section asks for them. Forms are hand-rolled with no form library, although the brief only says 'where they fit'.
evidence.correctness: Validation is solid: trimmed name, max length, email regex, guests must be an integer from 1 to 8, and numeric strings are accepted (app.js:49-64). Fully booked and 'Only n seats left' are separate messages. The check and the push are synchronous on Node's single thread, so concurrent requests cannot oversell; this is tested (api.test.js:59-66). Cancel splices the booking out, so seats are recomputed (app.js:131), and the confirmation page for a cancelled reference shows 'not found or was cancelled'. After a 422 the form refreshes seats (Book.jsx:43). Weaknesses: Staff.jsx:65-71 cancel() has no try/catch, so a network failure gives an unhandled rejection and no feedback. Cancel takes effect immediately with no confirmation step. Bookings are kept only in memory (allowed by the brief).
evidence.security: The password check uses timingSafeEqual over SHA-256 digests, and sign-in is refused when STAFF_PASSWORD is empty (app.js:95-96). The session is regenerated on login and destroyed on logout (app.js:98-109). The cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure on 'auto' and lasts 2 hours, and the session secret is random per process (app.js:30-36). Failed logins are rate limited (app.js:84-91). Helmet sets a CSP, and the JSON body is limited to 10kb. The staff API is guarded by requireStaff. React escapes all output, and there are no secrets in the code. The public confirmation endpoint deliberately omits name and email (app.js:77-82). Only minor concerns remain: the lockout can be triggered by others, and the session store is in memory.
evidence.code_quality: The structure is small and clear: server/app.js (factory, testable), index.js (env), tastings.js, and the pages split by route. Naming is good and error handling is consistent (422 with an errors map, a central error handler at app.js:143-146). There is no needless abstraction; the render-prop Field component (Book.jsx:5-14) is slightly clever but fine. Minor issues: the confirmation helper is declared after its first use inside a route closure (app.js:72), and api.js mixes fetch with formatting helpers.
evidence.tests: api.test.js has 25 meaningful supertest cases covering the listing, totals, seat reduction, the never-oversell rule, the concurrent-request case, invalid inputs (0, 9, 1.5, 'abc', blank name, bad email), unknown tasting, auth refusal, wrong password, unset password, lockout, cookie flags, listing and cancel-frees-seats, and logout. There are no frontend or end-to-end tests at all. The brief's UI contract (button 'Book <title>', labels, error next to field, 'Booking confirmed' heading, staff 'Sign in' and 'Cancel' flow) is not covered by any test.
evidence.ux_design: start.jpg shows a clear card grid with day, title, date, price and a green 'n seats left' badge, plus a full-width wine-coloured CTA. Low-seat and full states are styled (styles.css:66-69, Home.jsx:49-50 'Sold out'). The form shows a live total and a seats hint, and the inline error is red with a red border (form.jpg). The confirmation is a clear green-accented summary (confirmation.jpg). The staff page is tidy, with booked/left counts per tasting (staff.jpg). There are no imagery or tasting descriptions, so the content is a little thin for a winery.
evidence.accessibility: Strengths: labels are tied to inputs with htmlFor/id, there is a skip link (App.jsx:27), and aria-invalid plus aria-describedby link each field to its error (Book.jsx:9). Errors carry an 'Error:' prefix (styles.css:89), and focus moves to the confirmation heading (Confirmation.jsx:16-18). Other good points: a visible focus ring, dl/dt for facts, table headers with an sr-only action header, role=alert for page notices, and the lang attribute. Gaps: field errors are not in a live region and focus does not move to the first invalid field after submit, so screen-reader users get no announcement. Every staff 'Cancel' button has the same accessible name with no booking context. The muted text #6b5d5f on cream is borderline but passes.
evidence.simplicity: There are 7 runtime dependencies (express, express-session, express-rate-limit, helmet, react, react-dom, react-router-dom) and about 600 lines of source in total. Nothing is superfluous, and there is no database or state library. The size fits the task.
evidence.maintainability: There is no README, docs, ADR or spec, and no staff manual. STAFF_PASSWORD and TRUST_PROXY are documented only in code (index.js:4-8). There is no CI configuration. A package-lock.json is present, but engines is '>=22' with no .nvmrc, and dependencies use caret ranges. The version is 1.0.0 with no release approach. Build and test scripts exist (package.json:9-14), and the API regression tests are good. Built dist/ and .playwright-mcp/ debug artefacts were shipped in the folder even though .gitignore excludes them. A new developer would have to read the code to learn how to run it and configure the password.
evidence.visual_design: The palette is coherent (wine #591a2b, cream, gold accent border, serif headings), the spacing is consistent and the badges are rounded (start.jpg). The same header, footer and panel styling carries across all four screenshots. It looks finished and fits a winery, though it is fairly generic: a CSS circle logo and no photography or texture.
evidence.layout: The start page puts the hero and then the three cards first (start.jpg), with a responsive grid (auto-fit minmax 17rem) and a mobile table-to-cards collapse (styles.css:110-119). On desktop the form and confirmation are 34rem panels aligned left, leaving the right half of the page empty (form.jpg, confirmation.jpg), which feels unbalanced. The staff page groups bookings per tasting clearly (staff.jpg). There is no overlap or clipping.
evidence.usability: Booking takes 2 steps (card CTA, then form, then confirmation). Guests defaults to 2, a live total is shown, a back link 'All tastings' is present, and the button is disabled while busy. The staff flow is simple, but Cancel acts immediately with no confirmation or undo, which risks deleting a guest's booking by mistake. The 'Staff' link sits in the public footer, which is fine.
evidence.reception: Guests would find the site trustworthy and pleasant (consistent branding, clear prices and availability, a clean confirmation with a reference). It lacks descriptions of what each tasting includes, any email confirmation, and imagery, so it feels more like a booking widget than the winery's own site. Staff would find the bookings view clear.

unmet_requirements: Process: no spec, plan or design artefacts delivered despite the brief requiring a full specify/plan/test-first process
Seats left shows 'Fully booked' instead of '<n> seats left' when 0 (minor, arguably acceptable)
Forms are hand-rolled with no form library, although the brief asks to use established libraries for forms where they fit (minor)
strengths: Robust, well-guarded server: the seat limit is enforced server-side and safe under concurrency, input validation is thorough, and cancelling frees seats (app.js:44-133)
Strong staff security: constant-time password comparison, session regeneration, HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict cookie, rate-limited login, helmet
Coherent, polished winery look with clear available, low, full, error and success states across all pages (start.jpg, form.jpg, confirmation.jpg, staff.jpg)
issues: No README, docs or CI: run instructions and the STAFF_PASSWORD/TRUST_PROXY configuration are discoverable only from code, the Node version is not pinned, and build/debug artefacts (dist/, .playwright-mcp/) were shipped
No UI or end-to-end tests: the brief's interface contract (button and label texts, inline errors, confirmation heading, staff sign-in and cancel flow) is untested

Staff Cancel deletes a booking immediately with no confirmation, has no error handling for network failures (Staff.jsx:65-71), and every button has the same accessible name; form field errors are also not announced to screen readers
review.verdict: This is a well-built, secure and attractive booking app that meets essentially every functional requirement in the brief, with careful server-side validation and good API tests. It falls short on maintainability (no README, CI or docs) and has no UI tests or Cancel confirmation; I'd fix those before handing it to the winery.
